title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions and Mixed Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Add and subtract common fractions in which one denominator is a multiple of another; add and subtract mixed numbers; solve problems in contexts involving common fractions, including grouping and sharing.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 worksheets: adding and subtracting fractions with related denominators, improper fractions and mixed numbers. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Make the denominators the same, then add the numerators.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • With the same denominator, add or subtract the numerators.
  • When one denominator is a multiple of the other, change one fraction: 13 = 26.
  • Mixed numbers: add or subtract the wholes and the fractions, then regroup.
  • Write the answer in simplest form.

Examples

Example

34 + 58

68 + 58 = 118

Answer: 1 38

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding denominatorsKeep the common denominator.
Changing the bottom onlyMultiply the top too.
Not regrouping11/8 = 1 3/8.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about adding fractions?
faq.a: Add and subtract common fractions in which one denominator is a multiple of the other, and mixed numbers.
In Grade 6, one denominator is a multiple of the other, so use the bigger one.
Yes, write the answer in simplest form.

items.q:
The bar is split into eighths. Green shows 28 and yellow shows 38. What is 28 + 38?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. Add the numerators and keep the denominator: 2 + 3 = 5, so 28 + 38 = 58. The answer is 58.

items.q:
The bar is split into tenths. Green shows 310 and yellow shows 410. What is 310 + 410?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. Add the numerators and keep the denominator: 3 + 4 = 7, so 310 + 410 = 710. The answer is 710.

items.q:
The bar is split into sixths. The shaded part is 56, and 26 is crossed out. What is 56 − 26?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. Subtract the numerators and keep the denominator: 5 − 2 = 3, so 56 − 26 = 36. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 36 by 3 to get 12. The answer is 12.

items.q: Jabu wrote 25 + 15 = 310. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Fifths stay fifths. 2 fifths + 1 fifth = 3 fifths, so the answer is 35. Only the numerators are added. Also, 310 is less than 25, so it cannot be the total.

items.q: Which fraction is already in simplest form?
items.e: A fraction is in simplest form when the numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1. 410 = 25, 69 = 23 and 515 = 13 can all be simplified. 7 and 12 have no common factor, so 712 is in simplest form.

A 2 ℓ bottle of water is full. At the athletics day, Ethan drinks 34 ℓ and Zanele drinks 23 ℓ. How much water is left in the bottle?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add what they drink. Use twelfths: 912 + 812 = 1712 = 1 512 ℓ. Then 2 − 1 512: rename 1 whole, 2 = 1 1212. 1 1212 − 1 512 = 712 ℓ.

Give your answer in simplest form.

items.q:
Palesa has 3 13 m of ribbon. She uses 1 34 m to wrap a present. How much ribbon is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 3 13 = 3 412 and 1 34 = 1 912. 412 is less than 912, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 1212. 3 412 = 2 1612. Subtract the fractions: 1612 − 912 = 712. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 712 m.

items.q:
Karabo eats 14 of a pizza and Busisiwe eats 13 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: First add what they eat. Use twelfths: 312 + 412 = 712. The whole pizza is 1212. Left: 1212 − 712 = 512.

items.q:
On school camp, a Grade 6 class walks 2 14 km to a lookout and then 1 23 km to the campsite. How far do they walk altogether?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 3 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 2 14 = 2 312 and 1 23 = 1 812. Add the fractions: 312 + 812 = 1112. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. The answer is 3 1112 km.

items.q:
At cross-country training, Zinhle runs 1 34 km. Megan runs 1 56 km. How much further does Megan run than Zinhle?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: “How much further” means subtract. The lowest common multiple of 6 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the common denominator. Write equivalent fractions: 1 56 = 1 1012 and 1 34 = 1 912. Subtract the fractions: 1012 − 912 = 112. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 112 km.

items.q:
A damper recipe needs 34 kg of flour. Jabu has two bags with 12 kg and 18 kg in them. How much more flour does he need?
Give your answer in simplest form.
items.e: He has 12 + 18 = 48 + 18 = 58 kg. He needs 34 = 68 kg. 68 − 58 = 18 kg more.

items.q:
The swimming gala lasts 4 12 hours. Lunch takes 34 of an hour. How long is left for races?
Give your answer in simplest form.
c: 34 of an hour
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the common denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 4 12 = 4 24. 24 is less than 34, so regroup: rename 1 whole as 44. 4 24 = 3 64. Subtract the fractions: 64 − 34 = 34. The whole number left is 3. The answer is 3 34 hours. (That is 3 hours 45 minutes.)
